jane_acme: hey support, after I save a file with uvicorn --reload the redwood-py client starts hanging and subsequent requests time out. sometimes see `RuntimeError: Event loop is closed` in the worker logs. repro below.

sam_support: sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal repro and the uvicorn stdout/stderr? which redwood/httpx versions and are you creating the client at import time?

jane_acme: app is simple:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodAsyncClient
client = RedwoodAsyncClient(api_key="***")
app = FastAPI()

@app.get('/')
async def root():
    return await client.generate('hi')
```
Running `uvicorn main:app --reload`. after editing any file the reload happens and subsequent requests hang, sometimes `Event loop is closed` in logs.

jane_acme: pip freeze ->
redwood==0.12.1
httpx==0.23.0
uvicorn==0.20.0
python 3.10

eli_devex: creating async clients at import time + using `--reload` can leak loops and leave dangling httpx connections. try moving client creation into FastAPI lifespan (startup/shutdown) or create per-request if cheap. are you seeing this only in dev with --reload or in prod too?

jane_acme: just saw it locally with --reload, but also started seeing spikes in retries on our dev Redwood dashboard that look like real requests failing :grimacing:. not using gunicorn/preload.

sam_support: can you try this pattern?
```python
app = FastAPI()

@app.on_event('startup')
async def startup():
    app.state.rw = RedwoodAsyncClient(api_key="***")

@app.on_event('shutdown')
async def shutdown():
    await app.state.rw.aclose()

@app.get('/')
async def root():
    return await app.state.rw.generate('hello')
```
This ties client lifecycle to the process and ensures proper close on shutdown.

eli_devex: note `uvicorn --reload` uses a watcher process + a child. if you create the client at module import in the parent watcher it can get forked and cause loop/transport issues. avoid module-level clients when reloader/preload is used. for gunicorn set `preload_app=False` or create clients after fork.

infra-bot: Incident tracker created: INC-2026-855 (investigate event loop closed on reload)

jane_acme: I tried the startup pattern but still saw a slightly different error on quick successive reloads: `Loop is closed` coming from httpx internals when trying to close connections. stack shows `Task exception was never retrieved`.

sam_support: can you enable `PYTHONASYNCIODEBUG=1` and attach full uvicorn logs and the worker crash trace? also confirm your reload type (stat vs inotify) and OS.

jane_acme: attached logs -> snippet:
```
ERROR: Exception in callback BaseEventLoop.call_soon_threadsafe
handle: <Handle ...>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/lib/python3.10/asyncio/events.py", line 80, in _run
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/httpx/_client.py", line 412, in aclose
    await self._transport.aclose()
RuntimeError: Cannot close a running loop
```

eli_devex: two more things: 1) try upgrading `httpx` to 0.24.x and `redwood` to the latest patch (we fixed some close/cleanup races in 0.13.0). 2) as a short-term workaround avoid `--reload` or set the reload trigger to be less aggressive; the kill/start race under rapid file edits can reproduce the issue.

sam_support: if you can share a tiny repo we can run the same repro here. otherwise we'll escalate to eng-runtime. @eli_devex will take point on triage.

eli_devex: I'll add a small health-check that detects hung httpx clients and rotates the process as a fallback; also verifying we don't leak loop refs on client close. :thumbsup:

jane_acme: thanks — I'll try upgrade + startup lifecycle and share a repro if it persists. appreciate the quick help :pray:

deploy-bot: user jane_acme uploaded attachment: repro.zip

sam_support: created ticket ENG-8821 and assigned to eng-runtime. we'll update this thread when we have next steps.
